notes.title: Mouse/Touch Update + Cerebral Puzzle Showcase
notes.content:
A new update is out making the game fully playable using only a Mouse or a Touch input (ie. Steam Deck's touch screen), making the game more accessible.

Also, this week the Cerebral Puzzle Showcase takes place featuring lots of great puzzle games and Snakeloop is also getting its first sale with a 20% discount. You can check the event here : [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/CerebralPuzzleShowcase]https://store.steampowered.com/sale/CerebralPuzzleShowcase[/url]

[h2]Version d5 changelog[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Added Mouse / Touch input support to move Snakes.[/b] [i]Click/touch & drag to move Snakes.[/i]
[*] Swapped the position of Undo & Restart prompts in the UI.
[*] Undo move / Restart input prompts can now be interacted with Mouse. [i]Even when using Keyboard or Gamepad to move.[/i]
[*] Added a Pause button when using Mouse / Touch.
[*] When using Mouse / Touch, the Undo Move prompt shows up instantly after your first move instead of when Stuck.
[/list]

notes.title: Update #1 + Extra Levels (Workshop) + Sokoban Fest
notes.content:
The first update for Snakeloop is out, with mostly improvements to the workshop support and fixes some issues with cloud saving.

Also, I released Snakeloop's Extra Levels, a collection of 60 levels made during the development of the game and that weren't kept. They can be found for free on [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3453204992]the Workshop[/url].

And on other news, the game is part of Steam's Sokoban Fest running this week which features lots of puzzle games.

[h2]Version d4 changelog[/h2]
[list]
[*] It is now possible to update existing Workshop Levels. [i](through uploading again the same mod)[/i]
[*] First level of a mod will now be shown as the preview image in the workshop.
[*] Reworked Workshop Tags. Instead of "Single" & "Multiple" tags, there are now several tags based on the number of levels included within a mod : 1, 2-3, 4-6, 7-12 & 13+.
[*] Fixed Cloud Saves not loading correctly for levels progression.
[/list]

[h2]Snakeloop's Extra Levels (available on Workshop)[/h2]
During the development of the game, a lot more levels were created than the 90 that are available in the game and there's kinda no reason not to have them available for those who want some more levels to play.

So, I've released a collection of 60 levels that didn't made the cut for the game on the workshop. It's a mixed bad with both easy & hard levels alike and both original levels and variants of ones featured in the game. And they're available directly on the Steam Workshop:

[b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3453204992]Snakeloop's Extra Levels on the Workshop[/url][/b]

[i]To play those levels, you'll have to subscribe to them on the Workshop, then wait for Steam to download it, launch the game and they'll appear in the Extra Levels menu. You can also refer to the beginning of the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3447932578]Modding Guide[/url].[/i]

[h2]Sokoban Fest[/h2]
Snakeloop is part of Steam's Sokoban Fest running this week in which you can find a lot of similar puzzle games.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45294079/1b346bf5be21d805197fa7e4db8d92e51ecdcc02.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Snakeloop will release on March 28!
notes.content:
So, Steam Next Fest is coming to an end meaning it's the final stretch towards the release of the game.

And it's also time for the game to get a proper release date, so here's the announcement: [b]Snakeloop will release on March 28th[/b].

Next Fest went great and thanks to everyone who tested the demo. For some data, over 500 players played the demo so far, completing a total of over 10k levels, and also highlighting a couple points that needed improvement in the game.

The demo will remain available until at least the launch of the game and it is also getting a slight update to improve a couple things based on player feedback (changelog below).

Now, as to the full version of the game, it is pretty much 99% ready with the only things left being some refinement on the final selection & order of the 90 levels that will be available in the main game (rest will be added as bonus on the workshop), as well as finishing the support of the steam workshop for modding (structure for modding is already there, just need the workshop-specific stuff).
Also, the full game has a couple extra mechanics and twists that weren't showcased in the demo and will have significantly harder levels (as the demo was mostly the tutorial levels except for a couple levels).

[h2]Demo Version b4 Changelog[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added an "Optimal hint" showing how many moves above the optimal you are when you complete a level without the optimal solution. [i]This was requested by several players aIt. It can also be disabled in the settings if you don't want to care about the optimal.[/i]
[*] Move Counter is now enabled by default. [i]It was already there through the settings although could be easily missed.[/i] 
[*] Snake's tail color is slightly lighter on odd tiles. [i]This should make the difference between odd & even lengths pop out more, especially on screens with lower contrasts.[/i]
[*] "Undo" prompt text was changed to be more explicit, ie. "Undo Move" in English, "Retour en arrière" instead of "Annuler" in French, and so on.
[*] Move Counter setting name was changed in French & Spanish to be more explicit.
[/list]

notes.title: Steam Next Fest + Demo Update
notes.content:
[b]Snakeloop will be part of Steam Next Fest starting tomorrow.[/b]

The demo is also getting a small update, bringing a bit of QoL based on feedback and fixing a couple minor issues.

[h2]Demo Version b3 Changelog[/h2]
[list]
[*] Level Selection can now be accessed through the Pause menu or Level Complete screen.
[*] Fixed the optimization of E01 (21 moves -> 19 moves).
[*] Fixed the optimization of E03 (13 moves -> 12 moves). 
[*] Fixed the Levels' names not being localized.
[*] Quite a lot of optimization on levels loading, making it 2-3x faster for huge levels. [i]Although this isn't something that will be noticeable on any of the demo's nor the full game's levels as they remain relatively small but rather very large levels that could be created through modding. (iirc, full game's biggest level is 13x13 or 169 tiles while the optimization would only be visible upon loading that have thousands of tiles. Loading levels as big as 50x50 (2500 tiles) shouldn't cause any freeze,[/i]
[/list]
